investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T15:18–15:25Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for ~145–146 seconds until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are running on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod fails immediately with Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, effective capacity could drop to zero even without resource exhaustion.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across eligible nodes is too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workload. All three sibling checks failed with the same message within a 7-minute window, suggesting the resource was already exhausted before the first probe ran.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, preventing any new remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because the agent pod could never be created, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod times out (~146 s), and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling phase. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or incident signal is present; the impact is localized to this observability eval run.

All three sibling checks share the exact same scheduler message, strongly indicating a shared infrastructure constraint rather than an isolated eval defect.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. A misconfiguration or drift in node labels could reduce the eligible pool further.

TERTIARY — Stuck or leaked pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) did not terminate agent pods, those pods may be occupying the finite VM resource slots.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T15:18–15:25Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for ~145–146 seconds until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are running on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod fails immediately with Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no allocatable VM slots for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes; if those nodes are saturated there is no fallback, making the cluster effectively zero-capacity for this workload class.

Tertiary: A burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads (from users, other evals, or background jobs) may have consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots just before or during the eval window, causing transient exhaustion.

Lower probability: A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the effective pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes, both of which are now saturated.
